questions.question_text:
Which of the following is responsible for wearing out of bicycle tyres?
निम्नलिखित में से कौन साइकिल के टायर (Tyres) के घिसने (wearing out) के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
options: Magnetic force (चुंबकीय बल)
Frictional force (घर्षण बल)
Electrostatic force (स्थिर वैद्युत बल)
Muscular force (पेशीय बल)
questions.explanation: The continuous rubbing between the bicycle tyres and the rough surface of the road creates frictional force. Over time, this interlocking and breaking of irregularities causes the material of the tyre to wear out.
questions.distractor_rationale: Magnetic force requires magnets. Electrostatic force requires electric charges. Muscular force is used to pedal the bicycle, not what directly wears out the tyres on the ground.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand that friction causes wear and tear of surfaces in contact.
common_misconceptions: Tyres wear out just because they are old, not because of a specific force.
ai_context.hint: Think about what force is produced when two surfaces rub against each other.

questions.question_text:
Why is powder sprinkled on a carrom board?
कैरम बोर्ड (Carrom board) पर पाउडर (Powder) क्यों छिड़का जाता है?
options: To increase friction (घर्षण बढ़ाने के लिए)
To make the board look clean (बोर्ड को साफ दिखाने के लिए)
To reduce friction (घर्षण कम करने के लिए)
To give it a good smell (सुगंध देने के लिए)
questions.answer: To reduce friction (घर्षण कम करने के लिए)
questions.explanation: Sprinkling fine powder on the carrom board fills in the microscopic irregularities (valleys) on the wooden surface. This makes the surface smoother, reducing friction so the striker and coins can glide easily.
questions.distractor_rationale: Increasing friction would make the coins stop faster. Cleaning or smelling good are not the physics reasons for using powder in a game of carrom.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the concept of using a dry lubricant (powder) to reduce friction.
common_misconceptions: Powder acts as tiny wheels (rolling friction). Actually, it just fills the irregularities.
ai_context.hint: When you play carrom, do you want the coins to stop quickly or slide smoothly? What should happen to friction?

questions.question_text:
Arrange the following types of friction in increasing order of their magnitude (from weakest to strongest):
निम्नलिखित घर्षण (Friction) के प्रकारों को उनके परिमाण (Magnitude) के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें (सबसे कमजोर से सबसे मजबूत):
options: Rolling, Sliding, Static (लोटनिक, सर्पी, स्थैतिक)
Static, Sliding, Rolling (स्थैतिक, सर्पी, लोटनिक)
Sliding, Rolling, Static (सर्पी, लोटनिक, स्थैतिक)
Rolling, Static, Sliding (लोटनिक, स्थैतिक, सर्पी)
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is the weakest because the area of contact keeps changing. Sliding friction is stronger because surfaces slide over each other without enough time to fully lock. Static friction is the strongest because the objects are at rest, allowing microscopic irregularities to fully interlock.
questions.distractor_rationale: Static friction is always the highest because breaking the initial 'lock' between two resting surfaces requires the most force. Rolling friction is the least, which is why wheels were invented.

ai_context.learning_goal: Differentiate and compare the strengths of static, sliding, and rolling friction.
common_misconceptions: Rolling friction is stronger than sliding friction because wheels are heavy.
ai_context.hint: Why do we put wheels on heavy suitcases? Because it creates the weakest type of friction!

questions.question_text:
In which direction does the frictional force act on a moving object?
चलती हुई वस्तु पर घर्षण बल (Frictional force) किस दिशा में कार्य करता है?
options: In the direction of motion (गति की दिशा में)
Perpendicular to the motion (गति के लंबवत)
Opposite to the direction of motion (गति की दिशा के विपरीत)
Downward due to gravity (गुरुत्वाकर्षण के कारण नीचे की ओर)
questions.answer: Opposite to the direction of motion (गति की दिशा के विपरीत)
questions.explanation: Friction is a resistive force. It always acts in the direction opposite to the intended or actual motion of an object, trying to stop it.
questions.distractor_rationale: If it acted in the direction of motion, objects would speed up infinitely. Gravity acts downwards, but friction is parallel to the surfaces in contact.

ai_context.learning_goal: Remember the fundamental property of friction: it opposes motion.
common_misconceptions: Friction has no specific direction, it just surrounds the object.
ai_context.hint: If you slide a book forward, what invisible force pushes it backward to stop it?

questions.question_text:
Why do aeroplanes and birds have streamlined (special) shapes?
हवाई जहाज (Aeroplanes) और पक्षियों का आकार सुव्यवस्थित (Streamlined) क्यों होता है?
options: To look beautiful (सुंदर दिखने के लिए)
To reduce fluid friction or drag (तरल घर्षण या ड्रैग को कम करने के लिए)
To fly higher in the sky (आकाश में ऊंचा उड़ने के लिए)
To increase their weight (उनका वजन बढ़ाने के लिए)
questions.answer: To reduce fluid friction or drag (तरल घर्षण या ड्रैग को कम करने के लिए)
questions.explanation: Air exerts a frictional force called 'drag' on objects moving through it. A streamlined shape (like a teardrop or a fish) allows air or water to flow smoothly over the body, minimizing this resistance.
questions.distractor_rationale: While it might look elegant, the purpose is purely scientific (aerodynamics). A streamlined shape does not increase weight, and flying higher depends on engine power and lift, though reduced drag helps.

ai_context.learning_goal: Evaluate the necessity of aerodynamic shapes in overcoming fluid friction.
common_misconceptions: Only solid surfaces have friction; air does not cause friction.
ai_context.hint: Have you noticed how fishes and aeroplanes have similar pointy shapes? What are they trying to slice through easily?
